messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED PAGE: inference-gateway | high 5xx error rate detected (RPS 15% -> 48% 5xx in last 2m). PagerDuty: https://pd.example/INC123456 :siren:

pagerduty-bot: New incident INC123456 created and routed to #incidents. Detailed alert: region=us-west2, error=502/504 spike, affected-endpoints=/v1/generate,/v1/chat, approx 1200 errors/min.

Brian K: acked INC123456 :hand: (on-call)

Brian K: i'm jumping in. checking kube / gateway logs now. anyone see deploys in last 10m?

Maya S: not from infra. saw a small canary rollout 8m ago for model-edge v2 on dedicated pool but it was supposed to be limited. tagging eng-runtime.

Alex T: I see a surge of upstream 502s from inference-workers in us-west2, traceback looks like kvcache misses + connection resets to model hosts. logs: ```ERROR net/http: unexpected EOF
goroutine 2345 [running]:
  ... kvcache eviction race?```

Lisa R: Customer impact: a few premium customers report degraded generative API. Telemetry shows 42% of requests in us-west2 getting 5xx, global ~6%.

Brian K: rolling traffic away from us-west2 to us-east1 for aggressive slices. running: `curl -X POST https://routing.internal/slices/shift -d '{"from":"us-west2","to":"us-east1","pct":70}'`

ops-bot: routing change submitted, job id rjob-8971, expected convergence ~45s. :gear:

Maya S: can we pause the canary? alex, can you confirm which canary hosts are in the call path?

Alex T: yes pausing now: `kubectl scale deploy/model-edge-canary --replicas=0 -n inference` -> scaled. i'm also seeing spike in connection resets from model-host-12 and model-host-13.

incident-bot: Incident timeline note added by Brian K: paused canary + started slice shift.

Brian K: after slice shift, error rate in us-west2 fell to 18% then plateaued at ~10%. still above baseline. suspect lingering kvcache hotset thrash.

Lisa R: opened a customer status note in notes doc: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/INC123456 (brief). tagging support for outreach.

Maya S: can we temporarily enable 503->429 fallback for non-critical routes to reduce retry storms? we have a runbook snippet: ```# runbook fallback
set feature_flag:gateway_fallback=on
apply rate-limit 1200rps global
```

Brian K: applied gateway_fallback flag and tightened rate limits for anonymous routes. monitoring.

Alex T: also warming kvcache by prefetching top prefixes on remaining healthy hosts: `python tools/prefetch_kv.py --prefix-file common_prefixes.txt --hosts model-host-[1-8]`

ops-bot: kvcache prefetch job started (job id pre-334).

Maya S: good. i'll watch for the 5xx->ok slope and check for error regression in logs.

Brian K: PD note: INC123456 acked at 6321000600 by Brian K. Escalated to SRE lead if unacked after 15m.

Alex T: after prefetch and fallback, error rate in us-west2 dropped to 3.8% over last 2m, routing now at 30% to west.

Lisa R: customer impact reduced, no major incidents reported in last 10m. sending update to CX.

Maya S: keep on watch for 30m and we'll schedule a postmortem if it doesn't fully recover. initial hypothesis: kvcache eviction thrash exacerbated by canary hosts causing connection resets and a retry cascade.

Brian K: moving to monitoring state. leaving a runbook pointer and next steps in incident doc. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC123456 status set to monitoring by Brian K.

pagerduty-bot: INC123456 will auto-resolve if no new alerts in 60m.

Alex T: quick note for postmortem: add kvcache metrics (hit rate, eviction rate), canary routing config, and worker connection counts.

Lisa R: tagging support: @support-team please prepare customer outreach for impacted tenants (draft in confluence).

Maya S: thanks — I'll pick up the follow-up.

Brian K: signing off handover to Maya at 6321015200.
